title: Fintech startup Ramp hits $60 billion valuation after $1.85 billion funding round
key_facts: Ramp said it raised $1.85 billion in a primary financing round led by Dragoneer Investment Group, valuing it at $60 billion
Valuation was $44 billion in June, when it raised $750 million
New York-based Ramp provides corporate cards and expense management software; founded 2019
Says it has more than $2 billion annualized revenue and positive cash flow
Serves more than 85,000 companies with more than $275 billion annualized purchase volume, up 175% from a year earlier
Adding AI tools including software to monitor AI spending and optimize the cost of running AI models
Co-leads: Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, Avenir Growth; about $5 billion raised in total equity
quote_evidence: Financial technology startup Ramp said on Thursday it had raised $1.85 billion in a primary financing round led by Dragoneer Investment Group, valuing the company at $60 billion, as the company expands its artificial intelligence offerings.
Ramp's valuation marks a rise from $44 billion in June, when it raised $750 million in a funding round.
The company is also expanding into artificial intelligence tools, including software to monitor AI spending and optimize the cost of running AI models.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors keep paying large sums for finance software that adds AI.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); read the Reuters wire text on Central Oregon Daily. Revenue and volume figures are Ramp's own.
